newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN SOCCER FANS PROBED FOR ALLEGED EXTORTION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN SOCCER FANS PROBED FOR ALLEGED EXTORTION.

text.p: Nine fans of Italian first division soccer side AS Roma are being investigated on suspicion of offences including attempted extortion against the club, judicial sources in Rome said on Tuesday.
They said six of the fans, who have not so far been charged, had been confined to house arrest since September 27. The restrictive measures were renewed by a court on Monday.
Three other supporters are under orders to report to police twice a week, including one who was released from house arrest last week so he could attend school, the sources said.
The nine, all male, are being investigated by prosecuting magistrate Vincenzo Roselli, who is probing alleged offences that range from extortion and theft to menacing behaviour.

Three of the supporters are suspected of having used menaces against club officials and two tour operators to try to obtain cut-price travel and tickets for Roma's UEFA Cup quarter-final away leg against Czech side Slavia Prague last March.
Roma vice-president Giovanni Ferreri said the club had not instigated legal proceedings. He told Reuters he was confident that no concessions had been made.
"I have the utmost certainty that AS Roma do not give away free tickets or offer cheap tickets to anyone," Ferreri said.
The sports newspaper Corriere dello Sport last week carried a detailed article on the case, including transcripts of police telephone taps.

It quoted one of the fans under house arrest as threatening in a telephone conversation with a Roma official to hire a plane and take 200 supporters to the Prague game and "smash up the stadium" unless they got tickets.
The newspaper said seven of the fans were extremist hard-right sympathisers known as "Ultras".

Roselli is also investigating suspicions that several of the fans threatened journalists from local radio and TV stations who wanted to work on the terraces during a Roma-Lazio derby match last February and demanded payment for rights to film.
